questions.q: What is the difference between data drift and concept drift, per the lesson?
options: Data drift is a shift in the statistical shape of input data; concept drift is a change in the actual relationship between inputs and the correct output
Concept drift is always caused by a software bug, data drift never is
Data drift only applies to text models, concept drift only to numeric models
They are two names for the exact same phenomenon
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes these clearly: data drift is about the inputs looking different, concept drift is about the underlying relationship itself changing.

questions.q: What is 'label delay,' and why does it matter for monitoring?
options: A deliberate security feature that hides model outputs from users
The time it takes a dashboard to refresh its charts
A delay in how long it takes to train a new model version
The gap between a prediction and when its true outcome becomes knowable, which means performance monitoring against ground truth runs on a lag
questions.explain: Label delay specifically refers to not knowing the true outcome right away (e.g., loan default), which means waiting for accuracy metrics alone is too slow.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say data drift detection gives an earlier warning than performance monitoring alone?
options: Performance monitoring is technically impossible to implement
Data drift only matters after a model has already failed
Data drift detection is always 100% accurate while performance monitoring is not
Input shifts can be detected immediately, long before the ground-truth outcomes needed to measure accuracy become available
questions.explain: Because label delay holds back true performance measurement, detecting a shift in the input distribution today is an earlier, complementary signal.

questions.q: According to the commonly cited rule of thumb in the lesson, what does a PSI value above 0.2 typically indicate?
options: A significant distribution shift, suggesting the model should be retrained or reviewed
No shift at all — everything is fine
That the model's training data was deleted
A guaranteed software bug in the monitoring pipeline
questions.explain: The lesson's stated rule of thumb places PSI above 0.2 in the 'significant shift, retrain or review' range.

questions.q: What does the lesson say should happen once drift is confirmed, before any other action?
options: Automatically retrain without checking whether concept drift has occurred
Immediately delete the model with no further review
Ignore it unless a customer complains
Investigate first, to confirm the drift is real and understand its likely cause before reacting
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly lists investigation as the first step — confirming and understanding the drift before choosing retrain, rollback, or pause.
